records.name: South Philadelphia Community Fridge
records.summary: Volunteers who keep community fridges stocked with donated food at several sites across South Philadelphia. The fridges are open around the clock for anyone who needs food.
records.what_you_do: Stock the fridges with donated produce and pantry staples, help collect food from grocers and restaurants, or host a food drive.

schedule.text: Fridges are open around the clock. Volunteers join through the group's volunteer form; the site gives no set shift times.

cost.text: Free to take food. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form linked from the About page, or bring food to any fridge
first_step.basis: The group asks the public to volunteer through an open form; the site does not describe training.

records.notes: Open Collective page says the collective is archived. It names its old sponsor, Open Collective Foundation, as shutting down, and says the group moved to a new fiscal sponsor (not named there). The donate link goes to hcb.hackclub.com, which may be that sponsor; not confirmed. The group's own site has no dated items, and its footer year is not used as evidence. Status is probably_active on the strength of the working site, but the newest dated item is an April 2024 Open Collective update, so verify before release. The Grays Ferry fridge at Universal Audenried High School has no street address on the site and is not in the locations list.

records.name: Germantown Community Fridges
records.summary: Neighbors who keep two sidewalk fridges and pantries in Germantown stocked, cook meals for them, and shop for groceries to fill them.
records.what_you_do: Clean the fridges on a sign-up shift, make sandwiches or cook meals to drop off, pick up donations, do a grocery run, or join a spring to fall garden crew.

schedule.text: The fridges are open 24/7. Cleaning shifts use an online sign-up sheet, and the group cooks meals a few times a month.

cost.text: Free to take food. Donations are optional, from $5.

first_step.how: Fill in the Volunteer With Us form on the website, or sign up for a cleaning shift on the linked sign-up sheet
first_step.basis: Open to the public with a clear form and sign-up sheet; the site does not say beginners are specifically welcome.

records.notes: Open Collective lists expenses and contributions dated October 8, 2026, with the year printed. A search snippet also showed a budget entry dated July 10, 2026. Fiscal host is Mission Forward, per the Open Collective page; checks go to Mission Forward with the group named in the memo. Social handles printed on the site (not recorded as URLs): Instagram and TikTok @germantownfridge, YouTube @germantowncommunityfridge159, Facebook germantowncommunityfridge. The site footer says 2024; not used as evidence. Both addresses match between the site and Open Collective. Sign-up links are a Google Form and a SignUpGenius sheet on the get-involved page.

records.name: Save the Academy Coalition
records.summary: Volunteers working to keep the public museum of the Academy of Natural Sciences open on the Parkway. The campaign says the doors closed on September 27, 2026, and it is pressing officials to change that decision.
records.what_you_do: Sign the petition, contact city and state officials, make flyers, collect personal stories, and join volunteer work for rallies, vigils and events.

schedule.text: Rallies, vigils and events are announced on the campaign site. A City Council hearing is set for Monday, October 26, without a year on the site.

locations.label: Academy of Natural Sciences museum (campaign focus)

cost.text: Free to join. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form linked from the campaign website, or sign the petition and come to the next public event
first_step.basis: Public volunteer form and public events are listed; the page describes no training or application.

records.notes: The campaign says it is not affiliated with the Academy of Natural Sciences or Drexel University. Dated items on the site with a year: a September 1, 2026 closure announcement and a Sunday, September 27, 2026 candle vigil and march. Other site dates have no year, and none was assumed. The site says the closure can still be reversed, so status may change quickly. Fiscal sponsor per Open Collective: Center for Philadelphia's Urban Future. The group's own email is not printed; the site lists a Drexel official's email and phone, which were not recorded. Recheck before the October 26 hearing and after it.

records.name: East Passyunk Opera Project (ePOP)
records.summary: A Philadelphia opera company that brings opera, musical theater and art song into neighborhood venues, with free or low-cost shows and free community concerts.
records.what_you_do: Attend a show or free community concert, join the mailing list, or support the work through its fiscal sponsor, Fractured Atlas.

schedule.text: No upcoming show dates were listed on the website when checked on October 8, 2026. Shows are announced separately.

cost.text: The mission is free or low-cost shows. Check each show for its ticket price.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list on the website, then book a show or community concert when one is announced
first_step.basis: Shows are open to the public, but the site listed no upcoming dates when checked.

records.notes: Love Notes 4 Philly is this group's Fractured Atlas project: a single concert on January 11, 2025, described as the final show in its series. It is used as a source here, not as a separate record. The website footer says 2020 and labels a special project recipient for 2024 to 2025; those years are not used as activity evidence. Status is probably_active because the newest dated show is January 2025. The site has an events page, but no upcoming events were shown. The site gives no volunteer or audition route. Singers are professional opera artists per the site; the interest tags are the closest fit.

records.name: SIFTMedia 215 Collective
records.summary: A Philadelphia support network for women-identified and non-binary filmmakers, with workshops, screenings and mentoring for media artists.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member or subscribe to the newsletter, then attend a workshop or screening. You can also donate to support the group's film projects.

schedule.text: Workshops and screenings are listed on the events page and held online and in person. Some listings show only a month and day.

cost.text: Event prices were not stated in the text read. Membership and donations are offered.

first_step.how: Subscribe to the newsletter or use the contact page to join, then attend a listed workshop or screening
first_step.basis: Public workshops and screenings are listed and membership is offered; the page does not say beginners are specifically welcome.

records.notes: The home page lists a BlackStar Film Festival 2026 recap. It shows a year but no month, so no last_sign_of_life is recorded. The Spooky Screenings listings show only month and day and were not used. The contact email comes from the Fractured Atlas project page, which is public; the group's own site prints no email. Fractured Atlas lists the group as a fiscally sponsored project, online workshops since June 2020. The site footer says 2024 and was not used as evidence.

records.name: Sawubona Creativity Project
records.summary: A South Philadelphia arts group that teaches acting, improv and theatre to adults, kids and teens, and holds family shows at its theatre space.
records.what_you_do: Take an adult class or workshop, sign kids up for a theatre class or summer camp, come to a family show, or hire the group's improv team for a school. Artists can audition for shows when they are listed.

schedule.text: Adult classes and workshops, kids and teen classes and summer camps, and family shows are offered. Check the website for current dates and times.

cost.text: Class prices are on the website. The Fractured Atlas page also mentions free workshops and family shows at the theatre space.

first_step.how: Sign up for an adult or kids class on the website, or come to a family show
first_step.basis: Open classes, camps and family shows are offered to the public with a clear way to sign up; the site does not say beginners are specifically welcome.

records.notes: The site presents classes, camps and shows as current but shows no dated items, so status is probably_active by the working-site rule. The 2021 founding year comes from the Fractured Atlas page and does not show current activity. Site policy: no refunds; class credits or transfers only when requested by email. The phone number carries a 856 area code, as printed on the site.

records.name: La Guagua 47 Community Arts Project
records.summary: A Philadelphia arts project built around a bilingual Puerto Rican musical set on a city bus, with free community workshops, cultural celebrations and live performances in parks and schools.
records.what_you_do: Join a free art-making workshop or cultural celebration, or come to a live performance in a park, school or festival.

schedule.text: Community showcases were planned for 2026 and a world premiere for 2027. The project page gives no months or dates.

locations.label: Parks, schools and festivals in Philadelphia

cost.text: Free community programs and workshops, per the project page. Check performances for any ticket price.

first_step.how: Follow the project on Facebook or Instagram to catch a free workshop or live performance
first_step.basis: Free programs exist, but no sign-up or contact details were readable, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The project's own website returned only its title line on both attempts, so this record rests on the Fractured Atlas project page, which describes the musical as in development and gives years only. Status is probably_active because 2026 showcases are planned; no month or recent dated event was found. Interest tags lean toward the Latino and Puerto Rican cultural focus stated on the page. Recheck for dated events once the website loads.

records.name: Project SAFE Philly
records.notes: Hidden as private: the Open Collective page shows no volunteer, meeting, event or direct contact, and its updates are shown only to contributors. The group's website (projectsafe.dreamhosters.com) did not resolve when fetched. Two May 2024 expenses on the page were both rejected, so they are not counted as activity. Instagram @safephila is listed and was not read. The group does peer harm reduction work with women and queer people. The owner may want to decide how harm reduction peer groups are handled. Revisit if a public way in appears.

records.notes: The Open Collective page says the collective is archived and no longer active. Last dated item: a cash distribution and contributions on April 2, 2023. The group's website (mutualaidphilly.com) could not be read because of a certificate name mismatch. Recheck the site before final hiding.

records.name: OpenPHL
records.notes: The Open Collective page says the collective is archived and no longer active. It shows no dated activity. Its tags say civic tech and meetups. Its only link is a GitHub page, which was not read.

records.name: Philly Jewish Music Festival
records.notes: A planned one-day festival in Philadelphia, described in future tense, with a fundraising page titled as a help-to-start campaign. No date, no own website, and no way to attend or volunteer on the page. A one-time event, so not recorded as a group. Recheck if a festival date is announced.

records.name: The Sonder Space
records.notes: A Fractured Atlas project for one dance production at Theatre Exile, May 31 and June 1, 2024. The campaign has ended. No own website is named and no ongoing program was found, so it is treated as a one-time event. Instagram @the_sonderspace was not read.

records.name: Harmonie Hall
records.notes: A Manayunk venue, built in 1891 as a German social club and singing hall, that hosts concerts, staged readings, film screenings, and workshops or lessons. It is a building and venue rather than a group, so it is not published. Its Linktree and Instagram (harmoniehall_1891) were not read. The page mentions workshops and lessons, so a closer look at its program may be worth doing later.

records.notes: Fractured Atlas campaign for a single immersive show, The Liminary. The page shows Los Angeles, CA. Not in Philadelphia.

leads_only.name: Walk Around Philadelphia
leads_only.note: Fractured Atlas project page describes facilitated walks and exhibitions in Philadelphia and a city-wide public program since 2020, but lists no walks, dates or sign-up. The group's own site refused connection on three attempts, so it could not be checked. Instagram and YouTube are listed on the Fractured Atlas page (not read). Recheck when the site loads.

leads_only.note: Fractured Atlas project page: 10 free workshops planned for Philadelphia students, ending in a showcase the week of Juneteenth (no year). No own website, no registration route and no dated activity, so not recorded as a group.

notes: Budget: all 4 WebSearch calls used, so the search budget is exhausted. About 46 of 60 fetches used. Records: 18 total, 7 publish, 3 hide, 3 not_a_group, 5 out_of_area. Open Collective: the search pages did not render, so coverage of Philadelphia collectives is incomplete. Search snippets also mentioned Funds Y'All Mutual Aid Philly (last update summer 2022, no URL seen), which was not checked. Fractured Atlas: no project directory was readable. Its fundraising site is mostly individual creative campaigns, so the Philadelphia projects here came from search results and may be incomplete. Not recorded: MiR Community (Open Collective, no Philadelphia mention on its page); Neighborhood Village Project (Open Collective, cohorts in several countries, no Philadelphia city shown); ENOUGH! Plays to End Gun Violence (national teen playwriting campaign, no city shown); Crossroads (a one-person solo performance project, skipped); Brown Girl Recovery and Tiger Hill Sanctuary (outside Philadelphia per search snippets, not fetched); Fractured Atlas campaigns with no location shown (Little Red Light Theatre, Ellie de Waal and Dancers, Flannau Duo and others), not checked. Duplicates: the Love Notes 4 Philly campaign is part of the ePOP record. Germantown's social handles were printed without full URLs, so they appear only in notes. Owner decisions to watch: Project SAFE Philly is hidden as private; Harmonie Hall and The Sonder Space are treated as not groups; Save the Academy is an active advocacy campaign with a City Council hearing set for October 26; the South Philadelphia Community Fridge status rests on its working site and an April 2024 update, so it is the weakest publish record.
